items.question: From whom must this teaching be carefully concealed in the mortal world?
premises: The teaching requires concealment
Concealment demands deliberate effort
The mortal world contains unworthy recipients
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden from the lowest people in the mortal world.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world from the lowest of men.

items.question: To what kind of recipient may this teaching properly be given?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching should be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the section emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text marks a chapter boundary
The section is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
The chapter is numbered fifth
items.inference: This marks the fifth chapter in the section emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the section that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: Through whose grace has the determination of the Kaula doctrine become known?
premises: The speaker claims knowledge
The knowledge concerns the Kaula determination
The knowledge arose through another's grace
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
items.plain_english: O Lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of the Kaula doctrine.

items.question: What is the soul that has been declared, and what is its essential nature?
premises: The soul has been declared in teaching
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the declared soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what full explanation must be given?
premises: The soul undergoes dissolution
The locus of dissolution is unknown
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The teacher is asked to explain fully into what the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that soul?
premises: The soul is identified as supreme
The soul is partless and eternal
The soul is free from disease and stain
items.inference: The soul is supreme, partless, eternal, and utterly pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in relation to haṃsa and the individual power?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is also characterized as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.
uncertainties: The exact sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is doctrinally compressed.
items.plain_english: That soul who is supreme is indeed the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where does the breath-filled vital air abide within living beings?
premises: Vital air is filled with breath
This air is present in beings
Its presence extends to all living beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air abides in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is syntactically irregular.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The soul leaves the body
This departure is the decisive condition
A new designation is applied at that moment
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, the soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard
It is received in the ear
It comes down through an unbroken lineage
items.inference: This teaching is heard in the ear as it has come down through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge, O fair-faced one?
premises: The knowledge can be merely heard
Hearing alone constitutes a form of knowledge
This knowledge has efficacy
items.inference: Even mere knowledge heard is presented as efficacious.
uncertainties: The verse states the cause but leaves the effect implicit, completed in the next verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by this mere knowledge, even when only heard...

items.question: What practice over six months leads to a state free from bondage?
premises: Practice is prescribed for six months
The practitioner is described in relation to the ochre robe
The goal is freedom from bondage
items.inference: One who practices for six months attains a state free from bondage.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of kāṣāyaṃ is ambiguous in this compressed expression.
items.plain_english: But whoever practices for six months becomes free from bondage, beyond the ochre robe.

items.question: What condition and companionship result from the prescribed practice?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner gains association with yogis
Union with yogis is a valued outcome
items.inference: The practitioner becomes free from all diseases and attains union with yogis.
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, he attains union together with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching has now been fully communicated to Bhairavī regarding the soul?
premises: A teaching has been communicated
The teaching concerns the practice of the soul
Bhairavī is the addressed recipient
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been told to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has now been told to you.

items.question: To whom should this teaching be given based on inner qualification and resolve?
premises: The teaching may be given
The recipient must be endowed with all states
The recipient must have firm resolve
items.inference: This teaching should be given to one who is fully endowed and firmly resolved.
uncertainties: The phrase sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is open to doctrinal interpretation.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and whose mind is firmly resolved.

items.question: Under what condition must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs be withheld?
premises: The Kaula essence is highly valued
This essence originates from the yoginīs
Transmission is explicitly prohibited here
items.inference: The Kaula essence, born of the yoginīs, must not be given.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which has its origin in the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after the veil of ignorance is struck away?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A present transformation is declared
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: Today the body, once struck by ignorance, is declared pure.
uncertainties: The form deham appears accusative but functions as the subject in this context.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious teaching about overcoming time is now sought?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish to hear
The topic concerns time
The desired teaching is the auspicious deception of time
items.inference: The speaker now wishes to hear the auspicious means of deceiving time.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on the overcoming of time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through this teaching?
premises: The teacher promises to explain
Doubt is explicitly denied
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching is declared to destroy death without doubt.
items.plain_english: I shall tell you—there is no doubt—how death is destroyed.

items.question: What condition affects even the wise at the tip of nectar and essence?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
The essence acts as a burning agent
Even the wise are affected
items.inference: Even a wise person is described as burning at the tip of nectar by its essence.
uncertainties: The imagery is compressed and may have esoteric physiological meaning.
items.plain_english: Even the wise person is burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: How should the breath be drawn in at the root of the tongue and palate?
premises: A specific bodily locus is prescribed
The breath is to be taken in
The action must be done slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this breath discipline for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The practice becomes established
Old age and death are subject to destruction
items.inference: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.
items.plain_english: When this is practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protection against venom is attained in the body through this accomplishment?
premises: Poison normally enters the body
A bite by great serpents is a severe condition
The accomplished state prevents poison's entry
items.inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
items.plain_english: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body.
